text: concluded that autologous PBSC trans- plantation is safe for the majority of patients older than 65 years, and guidelines have suggested its consideration in this group3 if they have good functional status and limited co-morbidity. With tandem transplantation, patients re- ceive a second planned autologous HSCT,9 since it was shown that patients who did not enter remission after one transplant could achieve remission after another.10 Some recommend tandem transplants in those who do not have at least a very good partial response after the first,11 and as such, some centres routinely collect enough stem cells for two transplants.9,12 Allogeneic HSCT has been used for multiple myeloma, sometimes after autologous HSCT, but few patients are suitable, and transplant-related morbidity and mortality are high with conventional myeloablative chemotherapy regimens; non-myeloablative regimens (miniallogeneic HSCT) are under investigation.9-12 Patients may be treated with vincristine, doxorubicin, and dexamethasone (VAD) for 3 to 4 months before transplan- tation,11,12 although dexamethasone alone, or with thalido- mide, has become a standard induction therapy.2,9 Lipo- somal doxorubicin has been substituted for standard doxorubicin in the VAD regimen.2 Some recommend le- nalidomide with dexamethasone as standard induction therapy,11 and other options include bortezomib-based reg- imens.2,9,11 Oral induction with cyclophosphamide, idaru- bicin, and dexamethasone has also been tried.13 Peripheral stem cells are collected after giving high-dose cyclophos- phamide and granulocyte colony-stimulating factor.5,8 Al- though some suggest the use of alkylating agents and inter- feron alfa after stem cell collection,8 earlier alkylator therapy interferes with stem cell mobilisation,2,9,11,12 and can result in poor engraftment.6,7 The standard condition- ing regimen before transplantation is considered to be high-dose melphalan.3,5,6,8,9,12 Total body irradiation is no longer recommended, as combined with lower dose mel- phalan, it resulted in higher toxicity and no significant sur- vival benefit compared with high-dose melphalan alone.5-7 Similarly, stem cells are not purged of contaminating my- eloma cells as a randomised study14 showed no benefit. Where transplantation is infeasible or inappropriate, chemotherapy may be given to induce remission and pro- long survival.
